  "text": "Martin found the spare key in a tobacco tin behind the drainpipe.

His father had told him it was there, though not recently.

Inside, the house smelled of furniture polish. Someone had washed the cup beside the sink and left it upside down on a folded cloth.

His sister arrived carrying cardboard boxes.

“Books first?” she said.

“All right.”

They worked until noon. She wrote on each box before closing it. History. Gardening. Keep.

In the kitchen, Martin opened a drawer looking for scissors. There were batteries, string, a screwdriver with a split handle. At the back lay six brown envelopes, each marked with a year.

Inside the first were receipts for things his father had bought him: school shoes, a bicycle, a winter coat.

“What have you got?” his sister asked.

“Receipts.”

“Anything we need?”

He looked at the bicycle receipt. Beside the price, in his father’s small handwriting, was the word blue.

“No.”

She went back to the sitting room.

He opened another envelope. A repair to his first car. Train tickets. A deposit for a flat.

From the other room came the long tearing sound of packing tape.

“Tea?” she called.

“I’ll make it.”

He put the envelopes back and filled the kettle.

There were two mugs on the shelf and his father’s cup beside the sink. He reached for it, then took down the mugs.

His sister came in and leaned against the counter.

“Sugar?” he asked.

“You know I don’t.”

“Yes,” he said.

While the kettle boiled, he found the scissors and carried them through to the boxes."
